title: MCU-Wide Timing Side Channels and Their Detection
problem: Microcontroller SoCs without shared buffers or parallelism are vulnerable to SoC-wide timing side channels that leak information about victim memory access patterns. These timing channels have been overlooked by prior security analysis despite representing a real threat to microcontroller security.
motivation: Timing side channels in resource-constrained microcontroller environments are a critical security concern that requires new detection and mitigation methods.
method: The authors develop a formal method to systematically detect timing side channels in SoCs. They apply this technique to the RISC-V Pulpissimo SoC, discover a previously unknown attack variant that exploits memory access timing behavior, implement a conservative architectural fix, and formally verify that the SoC becomes secure against this class of timing attacks.
key_novelty: Formal detection methodology for SoC-wide timing side channels in microcontrollers lacking shared resources, revealing timing vulnerabilities in architectures thought to be immune.
contributions: Identification of previously neglected SoC-wide timing side channels in resource-constrained microcontroller architectures
Formal method to systematically detect timing side channels in hardware designs
Discovery of new attack variant exploiting memory access timing in RISC-V Pulpissimo SoC
Verification approach to validate timing side channel immunity after implementing mitigations

metrics.other: Formal verification of timing side channel immunity

limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
